articles.title: Juvenile striped bass maintaining average abundance in Virginia waters in 2026
articles.description: Preliminary results from an ongoing long-term survey conducted by William & Mary's Virginia Institute of Marine Science (VIMS) suggest that an average year class of young-of-year striped bass was produced in the Virginia tributaries of the Chesapeake Bay in 2026. Striped bass are an important top predator in the Chesapeake Bay ecosystem and a valuable resource for commercial and recreational anglers. The 2026 year class, representing fish hatched this spring, will reach fishable sizes in three to four years.

articles.title: Nanoscale tech tracks proteins inside living neurons to guide Alzheimer's and Parkinson's drug discovery
articles.description: A technology developed at The University of Queensland allowing scientists to observe how disease-related proteins behave inside living neurons will be used to advance early drug discovery for neurodegenerative diseases. The NASTIC (Nanoscale Spatiotemporal Indexing Clustering) platform, spun out into Brisbane-based startup Accretion Bio, enables researchers to study real-time biological processes in living cells across space and time at the single-molecule level for the first time.

articles.title: The HOP announces Daniel Caesar as Hoptoberfest artist
articles.description: On Monday, Oct. 19 the Hopkins Student Organization for Programming (HOP) announced that Daniel Caesar would be the artist for the University's annual Hoptoberfest concert, which will take place on Saturday, Oct. 31. The HOP also hosted an event Monday at the Bloomberg Student Center to announce the performance. In addition to their in-person event, the HOP also announced Caesar as the artist over their social media platforms. Ashton Dumar Norwill Simmonds, known by his stage name Daniel Caesar, is a Canadian singer-songwriter who is best known for his songs "Superpowers," "Get You" and "Best Part," the latter of which Caesar won a Grammy Award for, along with artist H.E.R, who is featured on the song. Caesar released his newest album, "Son of Spergy," in 2025. Additionally, Caesar also embarked on the Son of Spergy Tour this year and performed at Baltimore's CFG Bank Arena in July. In an interview with The News-Letter, junior Sanidhya Oli, majoring in Molecular and Cellular Biology, attended the HOP's reveal event and was excited about the announcement because she was not able to attend Caesar's previous concert in Baltimore. "I'm super excited. I know he came to Baltimore over the summer, and I was planning on going, so I'm happy that he's coming to Hopkins, and I'm glad that we've had a variety of artists throughout the past years," said Oli. Additionally, Oli said that she is planning on attending the concert and hopes to be able to stand in the front row. "I am planning on attending. I will definitely be barricade," said Oli. Junior Julia Messing, majoring in Medicine, Science and the Humanities, also attended the event and was somewhat disappointed by the reveal. "I've never heard of him, so I'm pretty unhappy. Whereas, like, I feel like all the other artists I've at least like heard of them or know a song, but I don't even know his most popular song. So [I was] a little bit disappointed compared to some of the rumors I heard," said Messing. However, Messing also shared that she still plans on attending the concert and is glad that the HOP is able to put on the annual concert, which is free for students to attend. "I still plan on attending. I'm just gonna study up, I guess. But I'm just happy it's free, so it gives students who don't necessarily know the artist the opportunity to attend without feeling burdened by cost, said Messing. Senior Rebecca Wu is the President of the HOP. Wu was in attendance at Monday's event. When asked how the artists for the annual Hoptoberfest and Spring Fair concerts are chosen, Wu gave some context into the process in an interview with The News-Letter. "We work very closely with the lead office to find prospective artists that we think the students might be interested in, and then we try to work with LEED to see who they are able to get in accordance with JHU policies," Wu said. Hoptoberfest is a University tradition that dates back to 2013. Previous headlining artists at the Hoptoberfest concert have included Khalid in 2025, Rick Ross in 2023, Desiigner in 2022 and the Plain White T's in 2018. Students will be able to register for tickets to Caesar's performance on Wednesday, October 21 at 12 p.m. The concert will take place on Saturday, Oct. 31 at 8 p.m. in the Ralph O'Connor Recreation Center.

They were discovered in 1974, and people have assumed they were built exclusively by men. But new research on this underground army and its chariots, horses and weapons suggests women and children lent a helping hand.

articles.title: Ancient Hox code reveals the developmental roots of vertebrate hind fins and limbs
articles.description: Paired appendages—the pectoral and pelvic fins of fishes and the forelimbs and hindlimbs of tetrapods—were a major innovation in vertebrate evolution. Their emergence greatly expanded the ways vertebrates could move through their environments and ultimately provided the developmental foundation for the evolution of limbs. Yet how the genetic system responsible for building paired appendages was assembled during evolution remains an unresolved question.
